request.system:
You are the test generator in Ledger. For one verified business rule of a legacy COBOL batch program you write test fixtures: complete, consistent sets of input records that exercise each branch of the rule and its boundaries. Every case is run through both the original COBOL program and a Python port, and their outputs are compared field by field, so a good case makes the rule's behaviour visible in the output files.

Guidance:
- One case per branch of the rule's When conditions, plus boundaries: values exactly at a limit, one cent over, a date equal to the limit and the day after, combinations of conditions where the rule says one result overrides another, zero and negative amounts where they matter.
- Keep each case small (normally 1-4 records per file) but complete: every file the program reads gets consistent records with matching keys, unless the case is deliberately about a missing record.
- Give values as strings: alphanumeric fields as text, numeric fields as plain decimal numbers such as "1250.75" or "-40.00" (no sign encoding, no padding). Omitted numeric fields default to 0 and omitted alphanumeric fields to spaces. Use the copybook field names exactly.
- Call check_fixture on each fixture before you submit it and fix every error. Warnings may be intentional (for example a card that is deliberately missing).
- Write 3 to 6 cases. In "expectation", say what the rule implies should happen; it is a note for reviewers, not the pass/fail oracle.

messages.content:
Program: CBACT04C. Input files and their record layouts:

TCATBAL: CVTRA01Y TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD (50 bytes)
  TRANCAT-ACCT-ID              9(11)
  TRANCAT-TYPE-CD              X(2)
  TRANCAT-CD                   9(4)
  TRAN-CAT-BAL                 S9(9)V9(2)

XREF: CVACT03Y CARD-XREF-RECORD (50 bytes)
  XREF-CARD-NUM                X(16)
  XREF-CUST-ID                 9(9)
  XREF-ACCT-ID                 9(11)

ACCOUNT: CVACT01Y ACCOUNT-RECORD (300 bytes)
  ACCT-ID                      9(11)
  ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS           X(1)
  ACCT-CURR-BAL                S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT            S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT       S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-OPEN-DATE               X(10)
  ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE          X(10)
  ACCT-REISSUE-DATE            X(10)
  ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT         S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT          S9(10)V9(2)
  ACCT-ADDR-ZIP                X(10)
  ACCT-GROUP-ID                X(10)

DISCGRP: CVTRA02Y DIS-GROUP-RECORD (50 bytes)
  DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID            X(10)
  DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD             X(2)
  DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD              9(4)
  DIS-INT-RATE                 S9(4)V9(2)
The program runs with job PARM '2022071800'. Account, cross-reference and disclosure group files are read by key, so every category balance's account needs ACCOUNT and XREF records.

Rule to test:
{
 "id": "BR-CBACT04C-003",
 "title": "Interest rate lookup by account group, transaction type and category, falling back to the DEFAULT group",
 "summary": "For each transaction category balance, the program reads the disclosure group record keyed by the account's group ID, the transaction type code and the category code, and takes the interest rate from it. If no record exists for that key, it reads again with the group ID set to 'DEFAULT' and the same type and category codes. If that second read fails, or the first read fails for any reason other than record-not-found, the program abends. Interest and fees are only computed when the rate found is not zero.",
 "given": [
  {
   "text": "The disclosure group file is keyed by account group ID (10 characters), then transaction type code (2 characters), then transaction category code (4 digits).",
   "fields": [
    "FD-DISCGRP-KEY",
    "FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID",
    "FD-DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD",
    "FD-DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD"
   ],
   "literals": []
  },
  {
   "text": "The interest rate in the disclosure group record is a signed number with 4 integer digits and 2 decimal places.",
   "fields": [
    "DIS-INT-RATE"
   ],
   "literals": []
  },
  {
   "text": "The lookup key is made from the account's group ID (from the account record), the category code and the type code of the current transaction category balance record.",
   "fields": [
    "ACCT-GROUP-ID",
    "FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID",
    "TRANCAT-CD",
    "FD-DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD",
    "TRANCAT-TYPE-CD",
    "FD-DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD"
   ],
   "literals": []
  }
 ],
 "when": [
  {
   "text": "The disclosure group file is read by that key for each transaction category balance record.",
   "fields": [
    "DISCGRP-FILE",
    "DIS-GROUP-RECORD"
   ],
   "literals": []
  },
  {
   "text": "A read that succeeds (status 00) or finds no record (status 23) is accepted. Any other status stops the program with an abend.",
   "fields": [
    "DISCGRP-STATUS",
    "APPL-RESULT"
   ],
   "literals": [
    "00",
    "23",
    "ERROR READING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE"
   ]
  }
 ],
 "then": [
  {
   "text": "If a record is found for the exact key, its interest rate is the one used.",
   "fields": [
    "DIS-GROUP-RECORD"
   ],
   "literals": []
  },
  {
   "text": "If no record is found (status 23), only the group ID in the key is replaced with 'DEFAULT'. The same transaction type and category codes are kept, and the record is read again.",
   "fields": [
    "DISCGRP-STATUS",
    "FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID"
   ],
   "literals": [
    "23",
    "DEFAULT"
   ]
  },
  {
   "text": "The rate from the DEFAULT record is then used. If the DEFAULT read does not return status 00 (including when no DEFAULT record exists for that type and category), the program abends.",
   "fields": [
    "DIS-GROUP-RECORD",
    "DISCGRP-STATUS",
    "APPL-RESULT"
   ],
   "literals": [
    "00",
    "ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP"
   ]
  },
  {
   "text": "Interest and fees are computed for this category balance only when the rate found is not zero. A zero rate skips both.",
   "fields": [
    "DIS-INT-RATE"
   ],
   "literals": []
  }
 ]
}

condition.description: which branch or boundary of the rule this case exercises

expectation.description: what the rule says should happen (a note, not an oracle)

tools.name: check_fixture
tools.description: Encode a fixture with the copybook layouts and check field names, PIC fit, key uniqueness and cross-file consistency.
